summary:
PROMPT-007 completes the Finder operational layer.

Reports
- Reports stay in the shared moderation_report table, which gains a finder_category and two new typed targets, FINDER_REQUEST and FINDER_ACCOUNT, each with a text-compared CHECK and a one-open-report-per-reporter unique index.
- There are eight categories: false animal data, invalid chip claim, harassment, contract breach, unauthorized brokerage, cross-breed request, animal abuse and other.
- Each target is checked by the rule that already guards it. A person is reported only through a request both parties shared, never by account id, so the form cannot enumerate accounts.
- Private evidence uses FINDER_REPORT_EVIDENCE. Its signature is checked before anything is written; it is served only to FINDER_REPORT_MODERATE through its own route, and every view is audited.

Queue, decisions and appeals
- The queue shows the reported item alone: one message, a request status, or a masked person label. Numbers typed into the details are redacted.
- One moderator takes a report (conditional update). A decision needs a reason and an action allowed for that target; the action lands in the same transaction, and a conditional update allows only one decision per report.
- The affected person is notified and alone may appeal. A different moderator decides the appeal; overturning it restores the message or picture and lifts any sanction tied to the report.
- Marketplace appeal queries are now scoped away from Finder reports.

Blocks
- finder_user_block works both ways and is anonymous. The two people vanish from each other's profile pages and search, new requests, messages and forward commands are refused, and open pre-contract requests close with a neutral reason.

Sanctions
- account_sanction has two scopes and is superadmin-only.
- FINDER_ACCESS unlists the account's profiles (reason SUSPENSION) and refuses every new Finder action with a no-refund message.
- ACCOUNT also sets account.status to DISABLED and revokes every session.
- Neither scope touches subscription periods or creates payment rows, and lifting keeps the row.

Feedback
- Confidential feedback allows one note per party, only after the mating outcome is recorded. It is readable only with FINDER_FEEDBACK_VIEW, and there is no public rating.

Overview
- A counts-only overview (FINDER_ANALYTICS_VIEW) covers plans and rules, capacity, the request funnel, expiry, contracts, handoff, dates, reports, sanctions and notification health. Small breakdown groups are withheld.

Notifications
- Fourteen Finder and date kinds are added to the SMS catalogue with complete sentences that contain no record values.
- Chat message notices coalesce until the previous one is read.
- Reminders are deduplicated by finder_reminder, and their windows stay unset (off) until configured.
- The Phase 3 outbox deduplication, lease and retry are unchanged.

Reconciliation
- reconcileFinder is repeatable. It expires due requests, unlists profiles after a transfer, non-REGISTERED status, death, missing or archive, and unlists over-capacity profiles after a subscription ends (newest first, never one in coordination, nothing when the free capacity is unset). It also sends reminders and purges unused expired contract codes past retention.

PROMPT-006 gap closed
- The official_handoff and personal_handoff switches are now enforced.

newDatabase.note: abuse/queue races (take and decide), privacy (reported item only, redacted details, overview without identifiers), authorization (least-privilege capabilities, IDOR, enumeration), blocks, sanctions with session revocation and no refund, feedback, notification queue vs retry vs local send vs suppression, message coalescing, reminder dedupe, OTP secrecy and replay, contract access by operators, reconciliation idempotence and retention. Passed three runs in a row; re-run 9/9 after the marketplace appeal scoping fix.

checks.evidence: 1123/1124 in the full run; the release.test failure is the uncommitted prompts/ deletion and is verified on a clean worktree. The new suites pass 5/5 domain and 9/9 DB, and the affected existing suites pass 76/76.

274/275 in the full run. The one failure exposed the marketplace/Finder appeal scoping defect, which is fixed; both affected suites then pass 5/5 on a fresh build. A report with evidence goes through the queue take and reasoned decision; the evidence opens for the moderator and returns 404 for the reported owner. The appeal from the affected owner works at 360 px with no horizontal scroll, and after a block the profile is a 404 for the blocked person.

limitations: SMS delivery is verified only as queued, retried and accepted by the local test sender. No real provider was used, and 'SENT' means only that the local sender accepted the message.
CSRF protection relies on Next.js server actions' built-in Origin/Host check and a SameSite=Lax session cookie. No attack test was written.
reconcileFinder and the reminder sweep are not scheduled; they run from the superadmin button or from a job to be wired at deployment.
Reconciliation does not re-derive protected identity edits. The certification hook already unlists in the same transaction (PROMPT-003), and there is no identity snapshot to sweep against.
Unlisting a profile after an overturned appeal is not reversed by the operator; the owner re-activates it through the normal activation checks.
Message SMS is coalesced to one notice per unread burst. This is a deliberate compromise between the prompt and the Phase 3 catalogue rule (DEC-0223).
